questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had heard really good things about the TAFL center at Alexandria University

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Two of my subjects worked out really good and I feel like I liked coming to the classes and learned a lot! Unfortunately I can’t say the same about the Egyptian dialect class.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: All the formal things with visa and so on was easy enough. It was a bit more tricky with how to find a place to live, maybe TAFL could help the students a bit more there, maybe reach out to them before arrival and talk with them about options

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a PP presentation about life in Egypt and how to handle it, I think it was a little bit dramatic. We were also introduced to our studycalender and the rules at TAFL and I think that was also a bit over the top; fx that it said we would get minus points if we spoke English in class. In the end we could anytime ask a question in English and it wasn’t so strict luckily, so I think TAFL needs to relax a bit more on the first day and not scare the students like that

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Some of my class mates had gotten contacts from previous Danish students in Alexandria. I don’t know what we would have done without that. We ended up meeting a very nice broker that helped us find all our apartments and helped us during the whole stay. I’m sure those contacts will somehow be passed on to the next Danish batch going to Alex

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Do it! It’s probably cheaper and nicer

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to send some things to them before we arrived, it was pretty simple, and then we needed to get a student visa when we got down there, and we spend a few hours at TAFL + the police station in groups - it was very simple - we had a nice woman with us that told ud what to do

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Staff from TAFL

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I couldn’t choose the classes myself, but it was easy to register for them

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Relax:)) It’s all gonna be fine

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: 5 for the two subjects, 2-3 for the Egyptian dialect class

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Good level: very challenging but nice teachers and I ended up becoming really good on those 4 months - expecially in understanding and talking more freely and in longer sentences

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different teachings of Arabic. TAFL has some amazing methods, like we basically try to only speak in Arabic in class, we don’t use the dictionary but sinply try to use our own (small) knowledge to understand a poem fx and we use the root system a lot - and I think this is where the Arabic language is genious!

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: MSA, Egyptian dialect and Literature 1

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed Literature 1 and MSA but it was mainly because of my teachers. It is very nice to learn some Egyptian dialect but I would wish that the subject maybe took up less space/hours pr week and then was a bit more focused, more homework and smaller classes. It’s mainly a speaking class but I didn’t speak so much compared to my two other subjects. I didn’t feel like a really learned much more new knowledge after the first month or so. I think it went too fast with completing 3 books and I generally feel like the class wasn’t so good organized

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Remember to do something about your Danish simcard so you don’t pay double during the semester. Eating out can be really cheap and probably also cheaper than buying and cooking yourself. Make sure to bring some money for shopping nice glass, ceramics etc and go on trips to Cairo, Marsa Matruh, Siwa etc

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is generally extremely cheap

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was a part of the cooking Club and I was a bit disappointed that we don’t really do the cooking ourselves and don’t eat our own homecooked food…

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: 4 clubs I think: cooking, singing, caligraphy, Cinema

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Check out operas, events going on around the city. Fx at the French Institute, at the Library or the Anna Lindh Foundation

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Greek Club restaurant has a private Beach which is nice (cost 400 EGP I think) otherwise walk around Alex, go to the big fishmarket (that also has a lot of other things) 
Trips to Cairo, Marsa Matruh, Siwa, maybe Fayoum, Port Said etc

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy enough to follow the dressing rules and so on. But it’s generally very different than DK as you could expect so be prepared for that

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Consider to get a language partner, try to use some of the new words you learn in class when you go shopping or take a cab or something

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People wanting to take photos, shouting at you, maybe even sexually harassing you

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people are (most of them) very helpfull and hospitable

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
You are gonna improve your Arabic a lot!! 
It needs hard work!! 
Stay in Egypt and explore the huge diverse country it is - don’t spend your time travelling outside the country

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare to work a lot. During weekdays mostly busy the whole day with school and studying and also in some weekends. But also take your time to see the country when you have time. Expect the time to fly. Look forward for having probably the best teachers you’ve ever had!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: How much I improved my Arabic

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
All the homework 
The weather

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
